root_cause.text: In several ipset hash variants, the IPv4 range iteration loop increments the 32-bit iterator after processing the last address, causing it to wrap past the upper bound and resume from an unintended position on retry, leading to incorrect element insertion outside the requested range.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `ip++` from the `for` loop increment and adds a check `if (ip == ip_to) break;` before incrementing `ip` manually, ensuring the iterator stops exactly at the end of the range. The commit description states: "Advancing it once more can move the traversal state past the end of the request, so a later retry may continue from an unintended position."

    netfilter: ipset: Rework long task execution when adding/deleting entries
    
    When adding/deleting large number of elements in one step in ipset, it can
    take a reasonable amount of time and can result in soft lockup errors. The
    patch 5f7b51bf09ba ("netfilter: ipset: Limit the maximal range of
    consecutive elements to add/delete") tried to fix
bic_trace_step.reason: The loop `for (; ip <= ip_to; ip++)` increments the 32-bit `ip` after each iteration. If `ip_to` is 0xffffffff, `ip` wraps to 0 and continues, causing insertion of IPs outside the intended range. No guard against integer wrap is added. The retry mechanism saves and restores `h->next.ip` but does not prevent the wrap; when the loop breaks due to `i > IPSET_MAX_RANGE`, the saved next IP may be after the wrap, leading to incorrect resumption on retry. The vulnerable construct remains unfixed.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:

The range size of consecutive elements
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 5f7b51bf09baca8e4f80cbe879536842bafb5f31
Author: Jozsef Kadlecsik <kadlec@netfilter.org>
Date:   Wed Jul 28 17:01:15 2021 +0200

    netfilter: ipset: Limit the maximal range of consecutive elements to add/delete
    
    The range size of consecutive elements were not limited. Thus one could
    define a huge range which may result soft lockup errors due to the long
    execution time. Now the range size is limited to 2^20 entries.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit does not modify the vulnerable loop construct: `for (; ip <= ip_to; ip++)`. This loop increments a 32-bit IP iterator after processing the last address, causing wrap-around (e.g., from 0xFFFFFFFF to 0x00000000) and continued processing outside the requested range. The added range limit (`((u64)ip_to - ip + 1) > IPSET_MAX_RANGE`) does not prevent this wrap when the range is small but includes the maximum IP address. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present and not fixed.
